absent: Numeric values, bit positions, and capacity limits for reader protection flags, segment counts, loop counts, and pipeline length.
Contracts and side effects of operation helpers for mask selection, single extension, grace sequence sampling, polling, blocking checks, boosting checks, and callback queuing.
Layouts and lifecycles of the torture element, segment descriptor, random state, grace sequence, and per-processor accounting structures.
Behavior of scheduling, sleeping, timer, high resolution timer, cross-call, tick dependency, stutter, and stop-request helpers.
Implementation of callback offload helpers for parking, barriers, queue length checks, list handling, wait queues, and mask updates.
Meaning and defaults of configuration options and module parameters controlling logging detail, interrupt readers, up-down count, toggle interval, leak detection, and deboost checks.
Initial contents and concurrency rules for global error segment storage, preemption flags, online masks, and torture current pointer.

findings.text: The single read test record keeps polling control and grace progress markers together with the identity of the element under test and its current protection encoding. It provides storage for a bounded run of segment descriptors plus a cursor locating the next free slot and a local timestamp taken at entry. The layout allows one read operation to accumulate successive protection changes while retaining start information for later validation.

The up-down test record extends a single read record with timing and placement tracking for deferred completion. It contains a hard timer object, an in-use marker exchanged with ordering guarantees, requested duration and observed start values, the originating processor identifier, separate counters for started and completed operations plus migration events, a private random generator, and the embedded single read record. A global pointer holds the allocated vector of these records.

One torture read moves through preparation, protected access, optional protection reshaping, and validation. Preparation clears state and enters an initial protection. Access samples grace and time markers and acquires the current element, with an early exit when no writer is active. Reshaping appends further protection intervals when the current encoding permits extension. Validation samples completion markers, updates histograms, checks polling progress, releases protection, and preserves segment history on the first error or near miss.

The up-down test cycles slots between idle, armed, and completing. A worker claims an idle slot, records a down operation with an encoded protection value, and arms a hard relative timer for completion. The timer handler finishes the protected access, validates pairing of completions against starts, accounts for possible migration, and releases the slot. Initialization creates the slot vector and worker unless disabled or unsupported, while cleanup cancels pending timers and finishes orphaned accesses before freeing.

Callback offload control moves a processor record between offloaded and direct modes through a single toggle path. A request is ignored when already in the desired mode and rejected for online processors. On success the per-record transition runs and the global offload set is updated. Deactivation drains pending work, parks the callback worker, verifies empty queues, delegates list and flag handling to the grace worker with a wait, or performs flag clearing and unlinking directly when no grace worker exists.

Offload transitions observe an outer to inner order with processor-set read exclusion outermost, followed by a global offload mutex, then short critical sections guarded by grace or callback locks with interrupt masking. The interrupt-saving acquisition takes the callback spin protection only when the queue is marked offloaded, with an alternate build that only masks interrupts. Release mirrors acquisition by conditionally unlocking or only restoring interrupts. The deoffload completion predicate holds the callback lock while testing the offloaded marker to keep it stable.

Reader protection extension requires entry with an active protection and is skipped when the implementation reports a non-extendable encoding. Otherwise a randomized positive count of further intervals is appended, each chosen independently. Ordinary reshaping never introduces the dedicated up-down marker, which appears only on the path that records a down primitive result shifted and masked into the state together with that marker.

Grace polling is enabled for a small random subset of reads and its cookies are captured only when the active operation set supplies matching acquisition and query helpers. Start and completion sequence values bound each access and their difference plus the observed pipeline depth drive per-processor histogram updates with clamping to the pipeline capacity. A trace and dump are produced when the observed depth exceeds one, indicating an extended grace overlap.

Deactivation expects an offline target except for the early boot self case, an empty bypass queue and empty segmented queue after a full barrier, and stable flag handling while holding the relevant locks. Publication of the toggling record and clearing of the grace sleep indication occur atomically under the grace lock with a wake indication returned to the caller.

The reader worker runs until a stop request, repeatedly executing single reads with brief randomized pauses and honoring stutter control. When interrupt-driven reading is enabled and supported it maintains a one-tick timer and occasionally directs an asynchronous handler to another online processor with rate limiting. It also waits while the online population is below its assigned threshold or boot has not completed, and on exit it synchronously removes the timer and clears its tick dependency.

Two asynchronous entry points each perform one torture read with their own random state and account for their invocation. The timer path expects soft interrupt context without hard interrupt or nonmaskable context, while the handler path requires disabled interrupts and marks entry into a cross-call handler. Both attempt a non-sleeping allocation to exercise callback queuing when the operation set offers it, with the handler path omitting that exercise under proving or realtime builds.

The up-down worker scans the slot vector until stopped, skipping busy slots after checking for overdue completion and launching a new down operation on idle slots. Overdue detection compares current time against the recorded start plus a generous bound and warns once. Between scans it sleeps a randomized millisecond interval and honors stutter control, finishing with slot cleanup and a stopping report.

The offload toggle worker waits for boot completion, determines the highest possible processor identifier, and derives a fuzz bound as a fraction of the configured interval with a microsecond floor. Until stopped it selects a random target and direction, invokes the corresponding offload control, accounts for the direction, then sleeps the base interval plus random fuzz in interruptible state while honoring stutter control.
A public helper exposes deactivation of callback offload for a given processor by delegating to the generic toggle operation in the deoffload direction and returning its status.

Several one-time diagnostics guard against misuse and slow progress. They cover entry without active protection, exit with residual protection, polling queries that report completion, lingering pipeline depth when pointer leakage is enabled, continued task boosting after release with a dump of the recorded segments on first observation, unpaired completion counts in the up-down path, and timer completions that arrive far later than requested.

Deactivation mitigates races by parking the callback worker before inspecting queues, serializing toggle publication with the grace worker, and waiting for the offloaded marker to clear before returning. When no grace worker exists the transition clears the marker and unlinks the record directly under protection rather than waiting.

Segment diagnostics report a prefix of recorded intervals with per-interval timing when enabled, index and protection encoding, chained delay values that switch to additive notation after the first entry, optional processor and migration information, an optional grace range that collapses to blank filler when start equals end, optional millisecond and microsecond delays, a preemption note, and textual expansions for each active protection flag, followed by a global preemption notice when set.

Fresh single-read state starts cleared with polling enabled only on a rare random draw and the segment cursor reset to the base of the storage. Up-down initialization is bypassed for negative sizing or missing primitives and on allocation failure, otherwise each slot receives independent random state and a disarmed hard timer before the worker is created.

Named reader protection encodings, segment and loop bounds, pipeline capacity, timing conversions, and offload mode markers govern extension decisions, storage sizes, histogram clamping, and toggle behavior; their numeric values are not visible in these fragments and must be taken from the owning definitions.
